target.statement: Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 reaches F1 = 25.5% (Acc 55.7, Prec 77.6, Rec 15.3) on ATBench-C binary safe/unsafe trajectory classification.
target.table_ref: Table 2 (Main results on ATBench, ATBench-C block, row 'Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507')
target.dataset: ATBench (1,000 trajectories, 503 safe / 497 unsafe; ~9.01 turns, ~3.95k tokens each)

compute.basis: One 4B judge model must be run over all 1,000 trajectories averaging ~3.95k input tokens (~4M prefill tokens) on 8 CPU cores; a 4-bit 4B model fits easily in 16 GB and can finish in a few hours, but nothing about the run is small per-sample and the exact judge prompt template must be rebuilt if the repo is incomplete.

blockers: Top numbers (GPT-5.4/GPT-5.2/Gemini-3.x, 76.7% F1 headline) are closed-source API models and cannot be reproduced locally
Large open baselines (QwQ-32B, Qwen3-235B-A22B, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B) exceed 16 GB RAM/CPU-only budget
Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Llama-Guard-3/4 are gated on Hugging Face and need access approval
The exact LLM-judge prompt (stated to be the AgentDoG template) and guard native templates live in another paper's release; if the ATbench repo lacks them, scores are only approximate
Cannot verify from the paper text that the linked GitHub repo contains runnable evaluation configs for every baseline row
title: ATBench: A Diverse and Realistic Agent Trajectory Benchmark for Safety Evaluation and Diagnosis
